title: openai call-proxy: fragment stitcher and tool disambiguation hints
author: Priya Raman
description: Introduce a lightweight call-proxy adapter that sits between the OpenAI compatibility layer and Redwood's tool invocation surface. Motivation: models occasionally emit partial function/tool call fragments or provide ambiguous tool hints; downstream tool runners need deterministic, stitchable envelopes and deterministic tie-break behavior for multi-tool candidates. This PR implements: 1) call-proxy adapter that normalizes OpenAI function/tool call messages into Redwood's internal call envelope; 2) fragment_stitcher that incrementally coalesces streaming fragments into stable call payloads while preserving streaming progress events; 3) a new 'choice_hint' metadata field propagated from model signals to downstream router to express soft preferences when multiple tools match; 4) a conservative backoff+fallback policy when a selected tool returns transient errors (retry with alternative candidate or degrade to graceful error); 5) telemetry events for ambiguous selection and stitcher reassembly for debugging and regressions. Backwards compatibility: when openai_compat_mode is disabled the proxy is a no-op. Checklist: [x] call-proxy implementation; [x] fragment_stitcher core logic; [x] router integration for choice_hint; [x] unit + integration tests; [x] docs and changelog entry; [x] benchmark run and perf notes. Links: Linear ENG-2168 for rollout plan; ENG-2204 for telemetry schema changes.

release_notes: Added OpenAI call-proxy adapter and fragment stitcher: normalizes streamed function/tool fragments into deterministic call envelopes; introduces 'choice_hint' metadata for soft disambiguation between candidate tools; implements conservative backoff and fallback behavior for transient tool failures. Backwards compatible when openai_compat_mode is disabled. Note: minor perf overhead (~2% median token CPU) in hosted tier; rollout gated by feature flag for Dedicated/Private tenants.
